discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators (the quantum spin Hall effect)
rationale: Topological insulators are a field-defining condensed-matter discovery from the mid-2000s. They are heavily cited and have been recognised with the Breakthrough, Dirac and Oliver Buckley prizes. The pairing of the Kane-Mele theory with Molenkamp's 2007 HgTe experiment fits the Nobel pattern of crediting both theory and experiment. Recent prizes went to quantum circuits (2025), machine learning (2024) and attosecond physics (2023), which leaves room for a condensed-matter materials prize. Shoucheng Zhang's death removes a competing claimant and simplifies the citation.
